absent: Exact binary layouts and sizes of user FPSIMD, vector, and matrix state buffers and length negotiation rules.
Internals of per CPU FPSIMD context acquire and release and task binding helpers.
Streaming mode and ZA enable and preserve semantics beyond fallback no operation behavior.
Full task, thread, and register bundle struct definitions and fault field meanings.
Signal layout classification and delivery internals beyond forced fault injection.
Exception syndrome class table contents and notifier chain behavior.
Preemption, interrupt, nonmaskable, and stack pinning helper semantics.
Return address recovery for graph tracer and return probes beyond the callouts shown.
Console, taint, panic, and crash capture configuration and effects.
Endianness helper and fault tolerant copy internals for instruction reads.

findings.text: Kernel side floating and vector use is bracketed by begin and end helpers. Availability is tied to NEON support. Begin asserts task context, disables preemption, then enters a NEON region with no caller buffer. End leaves the NEON region with no caller buffer, then reenables preemption.

Permission for kernel SIMD differs by build variant. One variant requires finalized capabilities plus FPSIMD support plus absence of hard interrupt and nonmaskable context. The other variant always denies permission.

NEON begin first requires FPSIMD support and SIMD permission and nonpreemptible or explicitly buffered context, then takes per CPU FPSIMD context. If kernel FP state is already marked, it saves into the supplied buffer and expects soft interrupt service on non realtime builds. Otherwise it saves any live user state, records the caller buffer in the task thread area and marks kernel FP state except for task level soft interrupt overlap on non realtime builds, then flushes CPU state and releases the per CPU context.

NEON end is a no operation without FPSIMD support or without the kernel FP state mark. On non realtime builds in soft interrupt service it reloads from the supplied buffer and keeps the mark for the outer nesting level. Otherwise it clears the mark, checks the stored caller buffer against the supplied buffer, and clears the stored pointer.
This lane shows fallback Scalable Matrix Extension helpers. State size reports zero for the given task. Save requests a compile time failure. Entry from and exit to user mode are empty operations.

User FP state save starts from the per CPU last state descriptor and returns early when foreign state is marked. It preserves the FP mode register when supported. It selects Scalable Vector state when the pending save tag indicates current with vector thread mark or vector, and on Matrix Extension systems it samples the streaming vector control register, preserves ZA when enabled, and overrides vector selection with streaming length when streaming mode is active, with first fault register preservation conditioned on capability. Vector save stores vector registers plus common FPSIMD registers and tags the type as vector, otherwise it stores plain FPSIMD registers and tags the type as FPSIMD.

If the live vector length read from hardware disagrees with the length recorded in the last state descriptor during user save, the current task cannot safely return to user space, so the path injects an unrecoverable termination signal and abandons the save.

Fatal trap handling has a layered entry structure. Forced signal injection only proceeds in user mode and coerces misunderstood non termination signals toward termination before notifying. Notify records fault address and code in the current thread for user mode and forces a fault signal, while kernel mode enters the die path. Die serializes, enters oops state, reports, optionally triggers crash capture, taints, exits oops state, panics for interrupt context or configured panic on oops, then terminates the task unless a notifier stopped processing.

User mode is recognized by masking the saved processor state and comparing against the EL0 thread value. Compat user mode additionally requires the 32 bit flag together with EL0 thread value. The instruction pointer accessor exposes the saved program counter member.

Register display distinguishes compat and native tasks for link, stack, and highest general register index, prints processor state details in the matching 32 or 64 bit form, shows an interrupt priority mask member only on systems using that feature, hides kernel addresses behind hashed pointers while showing user addresses as plain hex, and iterates general registers in descending groups of three per line after a one line info header.

Backtrace dump ignores user mode register bundles, defaults a null task to current, requires successful pinning of the target stack, emits a call trace header at the supplied log level, walks with a per frame callback and the log level as cookie, then releases the stack pin.

Unwind setup builds a stack set from task plus CPU and optionally SDEI and EFI members, initializes common state with unknown stack and cleared flags, then selects one origin. Register origin requires the target to be current and seeds frame and program counter from the bundle. Caller origin seeds from builtin frame and return addresses. Other task origin seeds from saved thread frame and program counter. Iteration first recovers the return address, consumes one state per step, advances frames, treats missing entry as successful termination, and treats other negative results as failure.

Stack tracking uses low and high bounds plus a current stack and an array of candidate stacks with a count. Unwind cursor state carries owning task, optional register bundle, common frame and program counter, origin tag, and flag bits for graph and probe recovery. Task stack bounds span one thread size above the task stack page. Unknown stack is represented by zero bounds. Saved thread frame and program counter come from the thread CPU context.

The die path serializes on a dedicated die lock with interrupt state saved, enters oops handling, enables verbose console, brackets reporting with spinlock bustle markers, records a die taint with unreliable lockdep, exits oops handling, checks interrupt and panic conditions while still holding the lock, then releases before possibly terminating the task.

Frame unwinding rejects unaligned frame pointers, locates the containing stack first in the current stack then in the candidate set, requires the full record to lie inside strict bounds with overflow check and nonzero base, consumes the record by destroying the old stack entry to forbid backward transitions and raising the current low bound above the record, then loads the next frame and return address with single access semantics. A doubly zero record diverts to meta handling.

Unwind stepping clears flags then only accepts frame, caller, task, or register program counter origins and strips pointer authentication from the new program counter before return address recovery. Meta handling at an empty record distinguishes final versus register bundle types. Final only terminates successfully when it is the task top register bundle, otherwise it fails. Register bundle type consumes the whole bundle, reloads program counter and frame from it, clears the saved bundle pointer, and continues as register program counter origin. Unknown meta types fail.

CPU interrupt and overflow stacks are only exposed when the target is current and nonpreemptible, otherwise unknown is used. SDEI normal and critical stacks are only exposed when the target is current in nonmaskable context, otherwise unknown is used. The walker always includes task, interrupt, and overflow members and conditionally includes SDEI and EFI members by build configuration.

Task register bundle address is derived from thread size plus task stack page minus one bundle. Kernel address classification resets any tag then compares against the page offset boundary. Header guard and thread size define the associated layout constants.

FP state uses distinct tags for current, FPSIMD, and vector, plus thread marks for foreign state, kernel state, and vector enable, plus streaming vector control masks for ZA and streaming mode, plus unwind origins and meta types for final and register bundle records. Signal handling uses termination, illegal instruction, and memory fault numbers with a kernel fault injection code.

Kernel instruction dump only proceeds for TTBR1 addresses and prints a small window ending at the fault address. Each word is read with a fault tolerant helper that converts from little endian on success and prints placeholders on failure, with the faulting word visually distinguished.

Fault signal forcing shows the signal first, then uses plain forced termination for the termination number and fault style forcing with a user address otherwise. Display is skipped unless unhandled signal display is enabled and the signal is unhandled and a shared ratelimit allows it, and it reports task identity, exception class string and syndrome when present, the supplied reason, virtual memory area location of the program counter, and full registers.

Flushing CPU FP state requires FPSIMD support, clears the per CPU pointer to saved FPSIMD registers, stops streaming mode on Matrix Extension systems to avoid kernel NEON disturbance and excess power, and marks the thread as holding foreign FP state so later user save is skipped.
